sources.title: Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022
sources.locator: Complete 57-page notes; inspected PDF page markers 3–9 and 13–14. The stationarity and covariance definitions, finite-sample sample-ACVF formula and Gram proof are on PDF pages 4–9. The sample-mean variance identity and dominated-convergence summability argument are on PDF pages 13–14.

contents.name: PDF pages 4–5: strict stationarity by all finite-dimensional laws and weak stationarity by finite second moments, constant mean and lag-dependent covariance
PDF pages 4–8: mean/covariance conventions, the finite sample mean and the 1/n centered sample ACVF
PDF pages 8–9: zero-extended 1/n sample ACVF has nonnegative Toeplitz forms by a Gram factorization
PDF pages 13–14: double-sum sample-mean variance identity and dominated-convergence long-run variance limit under absolute summability
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the exact variance identity and the finite O(1/n) bound required by the current plan. The stronger long-run variance limit is recorded as source context but is not claimed.

contents.name: PDF page 3: stationarity alone does not justify averages; ergodicity is separately required
contents.reason: The notes flag that stationarity alone does not justify averaging. The local corollary states and proves the additional ergodicity, integrability and AC hypotheses for its almost-sure and L1 conclusion.
